newsitem.title: UK: UK deficit to meet Maastricht next year - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: UK deficit to meet Maastricht next year - Treasury.

text.p: The UK Treasury's financial statement and budget report (Red Book) said Britain's public sector deficit would meet the 3.0 percent of GDP Maastricht criterion next year.

The Red Book forecast the general government financial deficit (GGFD) at 30.5 billion stg, or 4.0 percent of GDP, in 1996-97 but said it would fall to 2.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997/98.
The GGFD is the measure chosen by the Maastricht Treaty.
The Red Book said Britain would also comfortably meet the Maastricht requirement that the ratio of overall debt to GDP must not exceed 60 percent.
The ratio of gross general government debt to GDP calculated for the Maastricht criterion stood at 53.75 percent of GDP at the end of March 1996, the Red Book said.
That measure is forecast to rise to 55.25 percent of GDP by the end of March next year, before stabilising and then declining.
